questiontext.text:
How is the Logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) defined?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

How is the Logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) defined?

The logarithmic function \(y = \log_a x\) is defined as the inverse function of the exponential function \(y = a^x\), where \(a\) is the base of the logarithm. In other words, the logarithmic function undoes what the exponential function does.

It is defined as for \(x>0 ,\,a>0\) and \(a \neq 1,\)

\(y = \log_a x \Leftrightarrow a^y=x\)

Additionally, it sketches the general shape of the graph of logarithmic functions \( y = \log_{a}x \) when \( a > 1 \).
